description: Keeping Toxins From Harmful Algal Blooms out of the Food Supply is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Center for the Humid Tropics of Latin America and the Caribbean; Group on Earth Observations; International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development. Dense populations of some microscopic algae (phytoplankton) in ocean waters can contaminate seafood, resulting in serious health problems for humans. Satellite data displayed in an online tool help fishermen monitor and avoid these harmful algal blooms. Coverage: the United States (2014). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Some phytoplankton species produce toxic chemicals, but they are not usually present at high enough concentrations to affect human or animal health. When populations of these phytoplankton species grow rapidly, however, they can produce large quantities of toxins and decrease oxygen availability in the water, posing a threat to marine life and humans that come into contact with the water....
